{{Documentation subpage}}

This template allows for numbered paragraphs using small text to the left of the paragraph text.

It is based on [[Template:Pline]], which is designed for line numbering in poems or plays. This template provides additional parameters for customisation.

Like [[Template:Pline]], this template makes use of anchored text. For example, [[Template:Numbered para 3#para1]] will link to a particular line.

== Usage ==
Note that in the below example, the margin has been set as <code>-3.5em</code>, overriding the default <code>-3em</code> since it would have overlapped with the green border surrounding the example.
{{doc example|
<pre>{{Numbered para 3|1|margin=-3.5em}} {{lorem ipsum}}

{{Numbered para 3|1|margin=-3.5em}} {{lorem ipsum}}</pre>
{{Numbered para 3|1|margin=-3.5em}} {{lorem ipsum}}

{{Numbered para 3|300|margin=-3.5em}} {{lorem ipsum}}
}}

I am aware the example looks a bit horrid. The intended use case doesn't involve borders.

== Parameters ==
{| class="wikitable"
! Parameter !! Description !! Default !! Example
|-
| <code>1</code> || Sets the paragraph number to display. This number is also used to generate an anchor ID.  

You can actually use any character you want in this field, including letters or special characters.

If left empty, no paragraph number is displayed.
|| <code>(None)</code> || <code><nowiki>{{Numbered para 3|8500}}</nowiki></code>
|-
| <code>id</code> || Sets a custom HTML anchor ID for the paragraph number, which will be highlighted when a user is linked to it. 
If left blank, the anchor ID will be generated using the format <code>paraN</code> where <code>N</code> is the displayed paragraph number. 
|| <code>paraN</code>|| <code><nowiki>{{Numbered para 3|8500|id=scary}}</nowiki></code>
Using the example from the previous row, <code><nowiki>{{Numbered para 3|8500}}</nowiki></code> will have an anchor ID of <code>para8500</code>.
|-
| <code>dot</code>|| Sets the symbol appended to the paragraph number. By default, this is the full stop.
You can actually use any character you want in this field, including letters, numbers, or special characters.
|| <code>.</code> || This is an example of appending a right bracket for numbering:
<code><nowiki>{{Numbered para 3|8500|dot=)}}</nowiki></code>
|-
| <code>size</code> || Sets the size of the paragraph number. This value accepts any valid CSS <code>font-size</code> value, including percentage, <code>em</code>,<code>rem</code>, or even pixels if you're fancy.|| <code>83%</code>|| <code><nowiki>{{Numbered para 3|8500|size=100%}}</nowiki></code>
|-
| <code>margin</code> || Sets the horizontal position of the paragraph number. Negative values move it further to the left, while less-negative or positive values move it to the right. || <code>-3em</code> || <code><nowiki>{{Numbered para 3|8500|margin=-3.5em}}</nowiki></code>
|-
| <code>color</code> or <code>colour</code> || Sets the colour of the paragraph number.
By default, this is set to black, or <code>#000000</code>. You can use any valid CSS colour value like <code>black</code> or even RGB.
|| <code>#000000</code> || <code><nowiki>{{Numbered para 3|8500|color=#2E8B57}}</nowiki></code> <ref group="note" name="once" />
|-
| <code>style</code> || Sets the font style of the paragraph number. This accepts any valid CSS <code>font-style</code>, like <code>normal</code>, <code>italic</code>, or <code>oblique</code>.|| <code>normal</code> || <code><nowiki>{{Numbered para 3|8500|style=italic}}</nowiki></code>
|-
| <code>weight</code> || Sets the font weight of the paragraph number. This accepts any valid CSS <code>font-weight</code> as well as numeric values from <code>100</code> to <code>900</code>, like <code>bold</code>|| <code>normal</code> || <code><nowiki>{{Numbered para 3|8500|weight=bold}}</nowiki></code>
|-
| <code>class</code> || Adds one or more CSS classes to the numbered paragraph element. You can use this to do some custom styling using your own CSS. 
The <code>numbered-para</code> class is always included.
|| <code>(None)</code> || <code><nowiki>{{Numbered para 3|8500|class=prettier_number}}</nowiki></code>
|}

== CSS ==
This template uses the following CSS:
<syntaxhighlight lang="css">
.numbered-para {
    float: left;
    text-align: right;
    min-width: 2.5em;
}

/* Based on Pline/styles.css by CalendulaAsteraceae*/
</syntaxhighlight>

You can override these rules using your personal CSS. The <code>margin</code>, <code>size</code>, <code>color</code> (or <code>colour</code>), <code>style</code>, and <code>weight</code> parameters control the corresponding inline styles. Other properties, such as <code>float</code>, <code>text-align</code>, and <code>min-width</code>, can be overridden through personal CSS.

This template's CSS is based on [[Template:Pline/styles.css]] by [[User:CalendulaAsteraceae|CalendulaAsteraceae]].

==Notes==
<references group="note">
<ref group="note" name="once">Because of unabashed pride in [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian%20English His Majesty's English], I've made this work when you use <code>colour</code> as the name for the parameter. In line with best practice for CSS, <code>color</code> also works and, perhaps unfortunately, takes precedence.</ref>
</references>
